newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet mechanics vote in favor of union.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet mechanics vote in favor of union.

text.p: In-house mechanics at ValuJet Inc. have voted in favor of representation by the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, the union said Wednesday.

The union said it was informed by the National Mediation Board, the federal agency that conducted the mail-ballot election, that 42 of the 70 eligible mechanics and inspectors at ValuJet voted for Teamster representation.

ValuJet resumed flying on Monday after being grounded for more than three months following a May 11 crash of one of its planes in the Florida Everglades that triggered an intensive safety review of its operations.

The no-frills airline was criticized by the Federal Aviation Administration after the crash for poorly overseeing the many subcontractors it used for aircraft maintenance. The FAA cleared ValuJet to resume flying last week.
The Teamsters said ValuJet's in-house mechanics sought union representation to increase their say in the company and expand the airline's in-house maintenance capability.
"This is good news for airline passengers," said Teamsters Union General President Ron Carey. "ValuJet needs steady experienced mechanics, not subcontracting of safety to the lowest bidder."
